doList: Lead with weekly savings, Monday offers, special offers, and clear calls to action such as “المزيد” / “shop now”.
Use Arabic-first messaging for Saudi shoppers, especially for promotions and store/service information.
Keep copy simple, direct, and price/promotion oriented.
Highlight core services shown on the site: Imtyaz loyalty, online shopping, weekly offers, Monday offers, and special offers.
When referencing the company profile, describe Farm Superstores as a Saudi retail and marketing company established in 1978 with headquarters in Dammam, if current verification is retained.
Use Saudi-market context and family grocery-shopping occasions.
dontList: Do not use overly luxurious or abstract lifestyle language that distracts from value, offers, and convenience.
Do not make unsupported superlative claims such as “the cheapest,” “the biggest,” or “the best in Saudi Arabia.”
Do not imply nationwide physical coverage beyond the regions stated on the site unless separately verified.
Do not present promotions as permanent; frame them as weekly, Monday, special, or limited offers where appropriate.
Do not overcomplicate Arabic promotional copy; keep it short and actionable.
Do not rely on English-only messaging for core shopper communications.
bannedClaims: “Lowest prices guaranteed” unless a formal price-guarantee policy is verified.
“Best supermarket in Saudi Arabia” or similar market-leadership claims unless independently substantiated.
“All products are always available” because offer and inventory availability can vary by branch/region.
“Free delivery” or “same-day delivery” unless confirmed for the specific online shopping channel and location.
Health, medical, organic, halal, or sustainability claims about products unless verified at SKU or program level.
Exact current store-count claims beyond the site’s wording of more than 100 supermarkets and 17 small-format stores unless updated and verified.
